findings.title: Cloud workload identity references an over-broad cloud role
findings.evidence: ServiceAccount of ServiceAccount/cloud-app (default) references the AWS AdministratorAccess policy 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AdministratorAccess'
findings.remediation: Replace the over-broad cloud role (AdministratorAccess, Owner/Editor/Contributor, or a wildcard role) with a narrowly scoped role that lists only the permissions the workload needs.

findings.title: Binding grants the cluster-admin role
findings.evidence: roleRef: ClusterRole/cluster-admin granted to ServiceAccount/superadmin (kube-system)
findings.remediation: Replace cluster-admin with a scoped Role that lists only the verbs and resources the subject needs.

findings.title: Binding grants the cluster-admin role
findings.evidence: roleRef: ClusterRole/cluster-admin granted to User/alice@example.com
findings.remediation: Replace cluster-admin with a scoped Role that lists only the verbs and resources the subject needs.

findings.title: Wildcard verbs in a role rule
findings.evidence: rule #1 of ClusterRole/god-mode (-): verbs=['*'] resources=['*'] apiGroups=['*']
findings.remediation: List the exact verbs the role needs (get, list, watch, ...) instead of '*'.

findings.title: Dangerous verbs: escalate, bind or impersonate
findings.evidence: rule #1 of Role/deploy-manager (default): verbs include ['bind', 'escalate', 'impersonate']
findings.remediation: Remove escalate/bind/impersonate unless the subject is a real RBAC administrator.

findings.title: Binding grants access to anonymous / authenticated users
findings.evidence: subject system:anonymous has access to ClusterRole/view
findings.remediation: Bind roles to named users, groups or service accounts — never to system:anonymous or system:authenticated.

findings.title: Privileged container
findings.evidence: container 'app' of Deployment/debug-app (default): securityContext.privileged: true
findings.remediation: Remove privileged: true. A privileged container is root on the host.

findings.title: hostPath volume mounted
findings.evidence: volume 'docker-sock' mounts hostPath '/var/run/docker.sock' — full host access (docker socket / root filesystem)
findings.remediation: Avoid hostPath. If a host path is truly needed, mount it read-only and only the exact directory.

findings.title: Pod Security Standards: capabilities.drop does not include ALL
findings.evidence: container 'backup' of CronJob/backup (dev): capabilities.drop is [] (restricted profile needs drop: [ALL])
findings.remediation: Add capabilities.drop: [ALL] to the container.

findings.title: Pod Security Standards: capability added other than NET_BIND_SERVICE
findings.evidence: container 'app' of Deployment/debug-app (default): capabilities.add includes ['CHOWN'] (restricted profile allows only NET_BIND_SERVICE)
findings.remediation: Remove the added capabilities; the restricted profile allows only NET_BIND_SERVICE.

findings.title: Wildcard resources in a role rule
findings.evidence: rule #1 of ClusterRole/god-mode (-): verbs=['*'] resources=['*'] apiGroups=['*']
findings.remediation: List the exact resources the role needs instead of '*'.

findings.title: Wildcard API groups in a role rule

findings.title: Role can read secrets
findings.evidence: rule #1 of ClusterRole/secrets-reader (-): verbs=['get', 'list', 'watch'] on secrets
findings.remediation: Scope secret access to the exact secret names (resourceNames) and the smallest verb set.

findings.title: allowPrivilegeEscalation is true
findings.evidence: container 'backup' of CronJob/backup (dev): allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
findings.remediation: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false in the container securityContext.

findings.title: hostNetwork is true
findings.evidence: spec.hostNetwork: true
findings.remediation: Remove hostNetwork: true — the pod shares the node's network namespace.

findings.title: hostPID is true
findings.evidence: spec.hostPID: true
findings.remediation: Remove hostPID: true — the pod can see and signal host processes.

findings.title: hostIPC is true
findings.evidence: spec.hostIPC: true
findings.remediation: Remove hostIPC: true — the pod shares the node's IPC namespace.

findings.title: Container can run as root (runAsNonRoot not set)
findings.evidence: container 'backup' of CronJob/backup (dev): runAsNonRoot is None, runAsUser is None
findings.remediation: Set runAsNonRoot: true (pod and container securityContext) and runAsUser to a non-zero UID.

findings.title: Dangerous Linux capability added
findings.evidence: container 'app' of Deployment/debug-app (default): capabilities.add includes ['NET_ADMIN', 'SYS_ADMIN']
findings.remediation: Drop the capability. Drop ALL capabilities and add back only what the container needs.

findings.title: ServiceAccount is bound to a cloud workload identity
findings.evidence: ServiceAccount of ServiceAccount/cloud-app (default) carries AWS EKS IRSA annotation 'eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AdministratorAccess' — the pod inherits the cloud role's permissions
findings.remediation: Review the cloud identity mapping: the pod inherits whatever the cloud role can do. Scope the cloud role to the exact permissions the workload needs and no more.

findings.title: ServiceAccount is bound to a cloud workload identity
findings.evidence: ServiceAccount of ServiceAccount/gke-app (default) carries GKE Workload Identity annotation 'iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: app@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com' — the pod inherits the cloud role's permissions
findings.remediation: Review the cloud identity mapping: the pod inherits whatever the cloud role can do. Scope the cloud role to the exact permissions the workload needs and no more.

findings.title: ServiceAccount is bound to a cloud workload identity
findings.evidence: ServiceAccount of ServiceAccount/legacy-app (default) carries Azure AD Pod Identity (deprecated) annotation 'aadpodidentity.k8s.io/identity: /subscriptions/0000/resourcegroups/rg/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/legacy-id' — the pod inherits the cloud role's permissions
findings.remediation: Review the cloud identity mapping: the pod inherits whatever the cloud role can do. Scope the cloud role to the exact permissions the workload needs and no more.

findings.title: Deprecated cloud pod-identity annotation in use
findings.evidence: ServiceAccount of ServiceAccount/legacy-app (default) uses deprecated Azure AD Pod Identity (deprecated) annotation 'aadpodidentity.k8s.io/identity: /subscriptions/0000/resourcegroups/rg/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/legacy-id'
findings.remediation: Migrate from the deprecated Azure pod-identity annotation (aadpodidentity) to Azure Workload Identity (azure.workload.identity/client-id); pod-identity is retired and no longer receives security fixes.

findings.title: Image uses :latest or has no tag
findings.evidence: container 'app' of Deployment/debug-app (default): image 'nginx:latest' uses :latest or has no tag
findings.remediation: Pin the image to an exact version tag, e.g. nginx:1.27.4, never latest and never untagged.

findings.title: Namespace has workloads but no NetworkPolicy
findings.evidence: namespace 'default' runs workloads (cloud-worker, debug-app, ipc-pod, worker) but has no NetworkPolicy
findings.remediation: Add a NetworkPolicy for the namespace (a default-deny policy is a good start).

findings.title: Namespace has workloads but no NetworkPolicy
findings.evidence: namespace 'dev' runs workloads (backup, batch) but has no NetworkPolicy
findings.remediation: Add a NetworkPolicy for the namespace (a default-deny policy is a good start).

findings.title: Default ServiceAccount is bound to a role
findings.evidence: the default ServiceAccount is bound to Role/pod-reader
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for the workload and bind the role to it.

findings.title: Binding references a role that does not exist
findings.evidence: roleRef ClusterRole/does-not-exist does not exist in the scanned manifests
findings.remediation: Fix the roleRef name, or create the role — a dangling binding grants nothing today but breaks silently when a role with that name appears.

findings.remediation: Pin the image by digest (image@sha256:...) — tags are mutable, digests are not.

findings.title: ClusterRole uses aggregationRule
findings.evidence: ClusterRole uses aggregationRule with selector [{'matchLabels': {'rbac.example.com/aggregate-to-view': 'true'}}] — its effective rules expand at runtime — aggregates 1 role(s): ClusterRole/view-extra
findings.remediation: Aggregated rules expand at runtime — review the roles matching the label selector; the audit may under-report this role.
